# Serve a sandbox's tools over MCP and REST

## Intent

An agent or script outside a sandbox can use the file, search and shell
tools on the sandbox's working directory through the hub, with nothing but a
Parley credential: a harness that speaks MCP connects to one URL, and a
script calls two REST routes. The tools run inside the sandbox, so what they
can read, write and reach is what the sandbox allows, and the hub decides who
may call which of them.

## Goals

1. An MCP client given the URL `…/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/mcp` and a
   Parley credential lists the sandbox's tools and calls them, with no other
   configuration.
2. A script lists the tools with one `GET` and calls one with one `POST`.
3. A caller who may run commands in the sandbox gets every tool. A caller
   who may only read the workspace gets the tools that change nothing, and
   cannot reach the others by either route.
4. A second `code_search` call on the same sandbox does not build the index
   again.
5. Every tool call that ran leaves one hub event naming the tool, its
   outcome and its duration, and never its arguments or its result.
6. A sandbox whose profile names no tool server answers
   `404 tools_unavailable` on all three routes, and nothing else about it
   changes.

## Non-goals

- A `parley sandbox tool` CLI command. Scripts use the REST routes.
- `parley mcp`, the CLI serving Parley's own operations with code mode. It
  is PRD 19.
- Search, outlines and symbols on the hub without a sandbox. It is PRD 20.
- Building or publishing the tool server or an image that holds it. The
  operator's image holds `agentkit-tools`; it comes from the agentkit-go
  repository and its CI/CD.
- A held-open tool session per client. Every call is its own process in the
  sandbox, because the runtime's exec carries no input.
- MCP features other than tools: no resources, prompts, sampling,
  elicitation or server-to-client requests, and no MCP authorization flow
  (OAuth). The credential is a bearer token.
- Streaming a tool's output while it runs. A call answers when it ends.
- Events for the calls a `code_mode` script makes inside its one call.
- Any change to exec, files, logs or attach.

## Background

Parley's sandboxes (PRD §13, packages 44 to 48) give an agent four ways to
act in one: exec, file upload and download, logs, and a terminal. An agent
that runs inside the sandbox needs none of them. An agent that runs outside
has to build its own file reading, searching and editing out of exec and
tar streams, and each harness would do that differently.

agentkit-go has those tools: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`,
`list_files`, `find_files`, `search_files`, `file_outline`, `find_symbol`,
`find_references`, `execute`, `run_command`, the indexed `code_search`, and
`code_mode`, which runs a model-written script over the others. Its PRD 15
(`docs/prd/15-serve-the-tools-from-one-command-and-drop-the-sandbox.md` in
that repository, pull request 185, not built yet) adds the command
`agentkit-tools`, which serves them for one directory. This PRD uses three
of its forms:

- `agentkit-tools tools` prints the tool definitions as a JSON array of
  `{name, description, input_schema, output_schema}`.
- `agentkit-tools call --request <file>` reads `{"name", "input"}` from a
  file, makes the call, prints one JSON object (`ok`, `data`, `error`,
  `detail`, `metadata`, and `text` when the model-facing text differs) and
  exits 0 whether the tool succeeded or failed; it exits 2 for a request it
  cannot read.
- `--dir`, `--index-dir`, `--read-only` and `--timeout` select the served
  directory, where the search index is kept between processes, the set
  without `write_file`, `edit_file`, `execute` and `run_command`, and the
  bound on one call.

On the hub, every route that uses a sandbox passes one gate
(`internal/sandbox/use.go`): scope and workspace access, the no-widening
rule of SBX-FR-012 for routes that act in the sandbox, the state check, and
the count of concurrent uses. The runtime client
(`internal/sandbox/runtime`) offers `Exec`, which runs a command and
collects its output, and `Upload`, which writes a file. The OpenShell client
refuses an exec with standard input, because the SDK's run takes none, so
the request of a tool call has to reach the sandbox as a file.

The hub has no MCP code today and `go.mod` holds no MCP module.

## Requirements

### Enabling: the profile names the tool server

A sandbox profile gains one field, `tool_server`: the absolute path of
`agentkit-tools` in the profile's image. The default is empty, which means
the profile's sandboxes have no tools.

- Static validation refuses a `tool_server` that is not an absolute path, or
  is longer than 256 bytes, with a message naming the profile and the key.
  The hub does not check at start that the image holds the file.
- `GET /sandbox-profiles` shows `tool_server` as a boolean, `tools`. The
  sandbox object gains `tools` (bool), a snapshot of the profile at
  creation like `image`.
- On a sandbox with `tools: false`, the three routes of this PRD answer
  `404`, `error_type: tools_unavailable`, after the scope and access checks.
- With the feature off (no `[sandbox]` section) they answer
  `404 sandboxes_disabled`, like every sandbox route.

### Who gets which tools

There are two tool sets. The **full set** is every tool the tool server
serves. The **read-only set** is the full set without `write_file`,
`edit_file`, `execute` and `run_command`, with `code_mode` bound to the
rest.

- A caller gets the full set when it would be allowed to exec in the
  sandbox: `sandboxes:write`, write access to the workspace, and a
  credential that covers the sandbox's hub credential (SBX-FR-012).
- Any other caller with `sandboxes:read` and read access to the workspace
  gets the read-only set. This includes a caller with write access whose
  credential does not cover the hub credential.
- A caller with neither is refused as on the logs route: `401`,
  `403 insufficient_scope`, `403 forbidden` or `404`.
- Workspace-bound tokens may use the routes, under the same rules.
- The set is decided per request. Listing shows exactly the caller's set,
  and a call to a tool outside it is refused before anything runs in the
  sandbox.
- The routes serve a sandbox in state `ready` only. In any other state they
  answer `409 sandbox_not_ready`.

### What one call does in the sandbox

For a tool call the hub writes the request to a file in the sandbox, runs
the tool server once on it, reads the result, and removes the file.

- The request file and the search index live under one directory outside
  the working directory, `/tmp/parley-tools`, so neither is ever part of a
  checkpoint or a commit. The request file is readable by the workload user
  only and has a name the hub chooses at random.
- The tool server runs as the workload user, in the working directory, with
  the sandbox's environment, as an exec does. It is given the working
  directory as the served directory, the index directory, the read-only
  switch when the caller has the read-only set, and the call's time bound.
- The request file is removed after the call, whether it succeeded or not.
  A failed removal is logged and does not change the answer.
- Arguments are at most 4 MiB as JSON; more is `413`. A result of more than
  4 MiB is a failed call (`tool_server_failed`, below).
- A call's time bound is the request's `timeout` (REST) or 10 minutes
  (MCP), cut to `[sandbox].max_exec_timeout`. When it passes, the answer is
  a tool result with `ok: false`, `error: "timeout"`.
- Each call counts as one of the sandbox's concurrent execs
  (`[sandbox].max_concurrent_execs`); one over the limit is `429`.
- Each call sets `last_activity_at`. Listing does not.
- The tool definitions are read from the tool server once per sandbox and
  set, and kept until the sandbox leaves `ready`.
- **When the tool server fails.** If it cannot be started, exits with a
  status other than 0, or prints something that is not one JSON object of
  the expected shape, the call (or the listing) fails with
  `error_type: tool_server_failed` and a message of at most 1,024 bytes,
  scrubbed as SBX-FR-064 says. When the runtime cannot be reached it is
  `sandbox_runtime_error`, as for exec.
- A tool that fails (a file not found, a non-unique edit, a command the
  tool reports as failed) is not a failed call: the caller gets the tool's
  result with `ok: false` and the tool's error code.
- The hub does not redact results: like exec output, a result may hold
  whatever the sandbox holds, exposed secrets included.

### REST routes

`GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools`

- Lists the caller's tool set: `200`
  `{"set": "full" | "read_only", "tools": [{"name", "description", "input_schema", "output_schema"}]}`,
  in the tool server's order. `output_schema` is null for a tool without
  one.
- Errors: the access errors above; `404 sandbox_not_found`;
  `404 tools_unavailable`; `409 sandbox_not_ready`;
  `502 tool_server_failed`; `502 sandbox_runtime_error`.

`POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name`

- Body: `{"input"?: object, "timeout"?: duration}`. `input` defaults to
  `{}`. `timeout` defaults to 60 s.
- Response: `200`
  `{"ok": bool, "data": object, "error"?: string, "detail"?: string, "text"?: string, "duration_ms": int}`.
  A tool failure and a timeout are `200` with `ok: false`.
- Errors: `400` for a body that is not such an object or a `timeout` that
  is not a positive duration; `403 insufficient_scope` for a tool of the
  full set called by a caller with the read-only set;
  `404`, `error_type: tool_not_found` for a name that is in neither set;
  `413`; `429`; and those of the listing.

### The MCP route

`POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/mcp` is an MCP server over Streamable
HTTP for that one sandbox.

- It is stateless: it sets and reads no session id, each request stands
  alone, and a hub restart between two requests is not visible to the
  client. `GET` and `DELETE` answer `405`. Responses are `application/json`.
- The credential is the request's `Authorization: Bearer` header, any
  credential the REST routes accept.
- `initialize` answers with the server name `parley`, the hub's version,
  the tools capability, and instructions of one sentence naming the
  workspace and the sandbox id. `ping` answers.
- `tools/list` answers with the caller's set: each tool's name,
  description, input schema and, where it has one, output schema, as the
  tool server gave them.
- `tools/call` makes the call as above. The result's `isError` is the
  negation of `ok`. Its text content is the tool server's `text` when
  there is one, and otherwise the JSON of `data` for a success and
  `<error>: <detail>` for a failure. `structuredContent` is `data` when the
  tool has an output schema.
- A `tools/call` naming a tool outside the caller's set, or unknown, is a
  JSON-RPC error with code `-32602` whose message names the tool. A failed
  call (`tool_server_failed`, `sandbox_runtime_error`) is a JSON-RPC error
  with code `-32603` and the scrubbed message.
- What is decided before the MCP message is read is answered as plain HTTP
  with the hub's error object, not as JSON-RPC: `401`, `403`, `404`
  (`sandbox_not_found`, `tools_unavailable`, `sandboxes_disabled`),
  `409 sandbox_not_ready`, `413` for a body over 8 MiB, and `429` for the
  rate limit. A `tools/call` over the concurrent-exec limit is a JSON-RPC
  error with code `-32000` and the message `sandbox busy`.
- Any other MCP method answers the protocol's method-not-found error.

### Events and metrics

- Every tool call that was started in the sandbox emits one hub event,
  `parley.sandbox.tool_call`, when it ends: resource type `sandbox`,
  resource id the sandbox id, the workspace's normal visibility, the
  caller as actor, the sandbox's `session_id`, and metadata
  `{"tool", "ok", "error"?, "duration_ms", "via": "mcp" | "rest", "set": "full" | "read_only"}`.
  `error` is the tool's error code, `timeout`, `tool_server_failed` or
  `sandbox_runtime_error`. Arguments and results never appear.
- A request refused before anything ran (access, state, limit, unknown
  tool) emits no event. Listing emits none.
- A `code_mode` call is one event, whatever its script called.
- Two metrics are new: `parley_sandbox_tool_calls_total`, by tool and
  outcome (`ok`, `tool_error`, `timeout`, `failed`), and
  `parley_sandbox_tool_call_duration_seconds`.

### End-to-end flows

1. **A harness outside the sandbox.** A developer creates a fork with a
   sandbox of a profile that names the tool server, and configures Claude
   Code with the sandbox's MCP URL and the fork's token. Claude Code lists
   thirteen tools, searches with `code_search`, edits with `edit_file`,
   runs the tests with `execute`, and pushes with `execute`. The hub's
   event stream shows one `parley.sandbox.tool_call` per call. The
   sandbox's checkpoint holds the edit and no index or request file.
2. **A reviewer.** An org member with read access lists the tools of a
   colleague's sandbox over REST, gets the read-only set, reads a file with
   `read_file`, and is refused `403 insufficient_scope` on `execute`.
3. **A script.** A CI script calls `POST …/tools/search_files` with a
   pattern and reads the matches from `data`.
4. **A profile without tools.** The same calls on a sandbox of a profile
   without `tool_server` answer `404 tools_unavailable`.

## Design Decisions

1. **The hub relays; the tools run in the sandbox** (owner's decision). The
   hub implements MCP and turns each call into one run of the tool server.
2. **One process per call** (decided after checking the runtime): the
   OpenShell SDK's exec takes no input, so a held-open session is not
   possible. The index persists in the sandbox to make that cheap.
3. **The profile opts in with `tool_server`** (owner's decision).
4. **REST routes beside MCP, no CLI command** (owner's decision).
5. **Read access gets the read-only set** (owner's decision). A caller that
   fails the no-widening rule falls back to it instead of being refused,
   because it may already read the sandbox's files and logs.
6. **One hub event per call** (owner's decision), without arguments or
   results, which may hold file contents and secrets.
7. **Stateless MCP with JSON responses.** It needs no session store, and
   hub restarts stay harmless (SBX-US-09).
8. **Constraint: the MCP protocol comes from the official Go SDK**
   (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`), which agentkit-go already
   uses, and is not written by hand. It is a new direct requirement of the
   hub.
9. **Fixed scratch directory `/tmp/parley-tools`**, not a profile field: an
   operator has no reason to choose it, and it must only be outside the
   working directory and writable by the workload user. An index lost with
   `/tmp` is rebuilt by the next search.
10. **The hub does not check for the binary at start**, because it would
    have to create a sandbox per profile to look. A profile whose image
    lacks it shows on first use as `tool_server_failed`.
11. **Timeout defaults differ by route**: 60 s for REST, as exec, since a
    script can pass its own; 10 minutes for MCP, where the client cannot.
12. **Works on any runtime**: only `Exec` without input and `Upload` are
    used, so a second runtime behind the same client needs nothing more.
    (Decision 14 adds `ExecStream` without input.)
13. **One package, profile `full`** (decided when the package was written):
    the work is six requirements and five tasks, the REST routes and the MCP
    route share the gate, the tool sets and the call, and neither is useful
    to specify without those.
14. **A tool call runs through `ExecStream`, collected by the hub, as the
    collected exec does** (decided from the code): the OpenShell client ends
    every operation that does not stream after 30 seconds, and a call may
    run for up to `[sandbox].max_exec_timeout`. Reading the definitions and
    removing the request file use `Exec`, which 30 seconds bounds.
15. **Listing takes no place among the concurrent execs** and records no
    activity: the PRD gives it no `429`, and it changes nothing.
16. **The tool server's command lines.** The definitions are read with
    `<tool_server> tools`, and with `--read-only` added for the read-only
    set. A call runs
    `<tool_server> call --request <file> --dir /workspace --index-dir /tmp/parley-tools/index --timeout <seconds>s`,
    with `--read-only` added for the read-only set. The request file is
    `/tmp/parley-tools/requests/<32 lowercase hex characters>.json`, with
    mode `0600`.
17. **`403` or `404` for a tool the caller may not call** is decided from
    the two lists of definitions: a name the full set holds and the
    caller's set does not is `403 insufficient_scope`, a name neither holds
    is `404 tool_not_found`.
18. **MCP arguments over 4 MiB** are a JSON-RPC error with code `-32602`
    naming the limit: a body under 8 MiB has passed the HTTP stage, so the
    answer cannot be `413`.
19. **A call whose caller leaves, or that runs when the hub begins to
    stop**, is killed as an exec is and gets no answer. It was started, so
    it emits its event, with `ok: false` and `error: "tool_server_failed"`,
    and counts under the outcome `failed`.
20. **A tool call is not an exec operation**: it is not told to the
    observers of sandbox operations and does not count in
    `parley_sandbox_exec_total`, since exec is not changed. Its record is
    its event and the two new metrics. The duration metric carries the
    label `tool`.
21. **The sandbox keeps the tool server's path**, in the snapshot of its
    profile, so that a later change of the profile does not reach a running
    sandbox. A sandbox created before this package has `tools: false`.
22. **The order of the checks** on the three routes is the gate's: the
    feature, the binding, the scope and workspace access, then
    `sandbox_not_found`, `tools_unavailable`, the body, the state, and for
    a call the tool's name and the place among the concurrent execs.

## Dependencies

- Packages 44 `sandbox_runtime_and_profiles`, 45
  `sandbox_creation_and_credentials`, 46 `sandbox_exec_files_and_logs`,
  47 `sandbox_lifecycle_and_checkpoints` (all active, every task done):
  the profile, the sandbox object, the use gate, the no-widening rule, the
  runtime client and the checkpoint this builds on. Their intent is not
  changed; the profile and the sandbox object each gain one field.
- Package 52 `durable_event_log_and_stream` (active, not yet implemented):
  carries the new event type like every other; this PRD does not wait for
  it.
- agentkit-go PRD 15 (pull request 185, not built): the `agentkit-tools`
  command and its `tools` and `call` forms. The hub's tests use a stand-in
  program with the same output; the end-to-end flow needs the real one.
- `docs/errata/46_sandbox_exec_files_and_logs.md`: `sandboxes:write`
  satisfies `sandboxes:read`, which the set rule relies on.

## Verified External API

`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` v1.8.0, package `mcp`, read with
`go doc` in the module cache (it requires `go 1.25.0`; the hub is on 1.27):

- `func NewServer(impl *Implementation, options *ServerOptions) *Server`
- `type Implementation struct { Name, Title, Description, Version string … }`
- `ServerOptions.Instructions string`
- `func (s *Server) AddTool(t *Tool, h ToolHandler)`: the input schema must
  be non-nil with type `object`; arguments arrive as `json.RawMessage` and
  are not validated by the SDK.
- `type ToolHandler func(context.Context, *CallToolRequest) (*CallToolResult, error)`
- `type CallToolResult struct { Content []Content; StructuredContent any; IsError bool … }`
- `func NewStreamableHTTPHandler(getServer func(*http.Request) *Server, opts *StreamableHTTPOptions) *StreamableHTTPHandler`
- `StreamableHTTPOptions.Stateless bool` (no session id; `GET` and `DELETE`
  answer 405) and `StreamableHTTPOptions.JSONResponse bool`.

Read the same way when the package was written:

- `type Tool struct { Name, Title, Description string; InputSchema any; OutputSchema any … }`:
  from the server, a schema may be any value that marshals to a JSON
  schema, `json.RawMessage` included.
- `type CallToolRequest = ServerRequest[*CallToolParamsRaw]`, with
  `Params.Name string` and `Params.Arguments json.RawMessage`.
- `type TextContent struct { Text string … }`, a `Content`.
- A `ToolHandler` that returns an error answers a protocol error, and one
  that returns `*jsonrpc.Error{Code, Message}`
  (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/jsonrpc`,
  `type Error = jsonrpc2.WireError`) answers that code. The package has
  `CodeInvalidParams = -32602`, `CodeInternalError = -32603` and
  `CodeMethodNotFound = -32601`.
- The server answers a `tools/call` naming a tool it does not hold with
  `-32602` and the message `unknown tool "<name>"`.
- `StreamableHTTPOptions.MaxRequestBodyBytes int64`: `413` over it; 4 MiB
  (`DefaultMaxRequestBodyBytes`) when left at zero.

**Unverified**: whether the server answers `resources/list` and
`prompts/list` with method-not-found when it holds no resource and no
prompt. **Not built**: `agentkit-tools`; its forms are as its PRD states
them, and the spelling of its flags in decision 16 is to be confirmed
against it.

## Glossary

- **Tool server**: the program `agentkit-tools` in the sandbox's image,
  which serves agentkit-go's tools for a directory.
- **Tool set**: the tools a caller may list and call: the full set or the
  read-only set.
- **Tool call**: one call of one tool through either route; one run of the
  tool server in the sandbox.
- **Failed call**: a tool call that produced no tool result because the
  tool server or the runtime failed. A tool result with `ok: false` is not
  one.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: The profile names the tool server

**Rationale:** An operator decides per profile whether its sandboxes offer tools, by saying where the tool server is in the profile's image.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHERE a [[sandbox.profiles]] table sets tool_server to an absolute path of at most 256 bytes, THE parleyd SHALL load the profile with that path as its tool server, and load a profile without the key, or with an empty value, as one without a tool server
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, extending TestFromConfig_ReadsEveryKeyOfAProfile and TestSettings_LooksUpProfilesAndCredentialsWithTheirDefaults: a profile table with tool_server = "/usr/local/bin/agentkit-tools" loads with Profile.ToolServer equal to it; a table without the key, and one with tool_server = "", load with ""; a path of exactly 256 bytes loads
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a profile's tool_server is not an absolute path or is longer than 256 bytes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the configuration with a message that names the profile and the key, and not start
   → the load of the [sandbox] section fails with a failure whose text holds sandbox.profiles[<name>].tool_server; the hub does not start
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/profile_test.go, new rows of the table of TestFromConfig_RefusesAnInvalidProfileNamingItsKey: tool_server in {"bin/agentkit-tools", "agentkit-tools", "./x", "/" followed by 256 bytes}: wantErrorNaming(t, s, err, "sandbox.profiles[agent].tool_server")
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN a caller requests GET /sandbox-profiles, THE parleyd SHALL show on each profile the boolean member tools, true exactly when the profile names a tool server, and never the path
   → HTTP 200; every item has tools: bool; no member of an item holds the tool server's path
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub with one profile that names a tool server and one that does not
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/routes_test.go, extending TestProfileList_ShowsWhatAProfileOffersWithoutItsPolicyPathEnvValuesOrSecrets: items[with].tools == true; items[without].tools == false; the body does not contain the path
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN a sandbox is created from a profile, THE parleyd SHALL keep the profile's tool server with the sandbox, in the snapshot of its profile, and show on the sandbox object the boolean member tools, true exactly when the snapshot names a tool server, whatever the profile says later
   → every sandbox object has tools: bool; the stored snapshot holds the path; no response holds the path
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/create_test.go, extending TestCreate_StoresProvisioningSandbox: a create from a profile with tool_server answers an object with tools == true and storedRecord(t, h, id).Snapshot.ToolServer == the path; a create from a profile without it answers tools == false. In internal/sandbox/object_test.go, extending TestObject_HasEveryMember: the object has the member tools
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any sandbox stored before the snapshot had a tool server, show tools: false and answer its tool routes as those of a sandbox without tools
   Check: unit
   - setup: a sandbox row whose stored snapshot JSON has no tool server member
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/store_test.go, extending TestStore_KeepsWhatItIsGiven: the row reads back with Snapshot.ToolServer == "" and ObjectOf(rec, true).Tools == false
   ```

### REQ-2: Decide who may use which tools of a sandbox

**Rationale:** A caller who may run commands in the sandbox gets every tool; a caller who may only read gets the tools that change nothing, and nobody else gets any.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a request to GET …/sandboxes/:id/tools, POST …/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name or POST …/sandboxes/:id/mcp comes from a caller that would be allowed to exec in the sandbox: its PAT, if it is one, holds sandboxes:write, it has write access to the workspace, and its credential covers the sandbox's hub credential, THE parleyd SHALL serve the request with the full set, every tool the tool server serves, decided for this request alone
   → the listing's set is "full" and holds every definition of `<tool_server> tools`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub with the fake runtime whose commands are answered by the stand-in tool server, serving thirteen tools without --read-only and nine with it
   - setup: a ready sandbox with tools and a hub credential holding sandboxes:write
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/tools_test.go, one table over callers, asserting the set of GET …/tools: {admin token: full; API key of an owner: full; PAT with sandboxes:write of a writer covering the hub credential: full; workspace-bound token of the fork with sandboxes:write: full; PAT with sandboxes:read of a writer: read_only; PAT with sandboxes:write of a member with read access: read_only; PAT with sandboxes:write of a writer that lacks a scope of the hub credential: read_only; PAT with sandboxes:write limited to paths the hub credential is not limited to: read_only; API key of a member with read access: read_only}
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN such a request comes from any other caller whose PAT, if it is one, holds sandboxes:read and who has read access to the workspace, a caller with write access whose credential does not cover the sandbox's hub credential included, THE parleyd SHALL serve the request with the read-only set: the full set without write_file, edit_file, execute and run_command, as the tool server defines it under --read-only

### REQ-3: List and call the tools over REST

**Rationale:** A script uses a sandbox's tools with one GET and one POST and no MCP client.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a caller with a tool set requests GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools on a ready sandbox with tools, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the caller's set and its tool definitions in the tool server's order
   → HTTP 200 with {"set": "full" | "read_only", "tools": [{"name", "description", "input_schema", "output_schema"}]}; output_schema is null for a tool without one; the schemas are the tool server's, member for member
   Check: integration

As a reader: set == "read_only" and names == the stand-in's under --read-only
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHILE a sandbox stays ready after the definitions of a set were read from its tool server, THE parleyd SHALL answer every listing and every call of that set from the definitions it kept, without running `<tool_server> tools` again, and read them again once the sandbox has left ready and is ready again
   Check: integration

   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any listing, leave last_activity_at as it was, take no place among the sandbox's concurrent execs, emit no event and count no metric
   Check: integration

[REQ-3.4] WHEN a caller requests POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name with a body {"input"?: object, "timeout"?: duration} naming a tool of its set, THE parleyd SHALL make the tool call with input, {} when absent, under the time bound timeout, 60s when absent, cut to [sandbox].max_exec_timeout when it is longer, and answer with the tool's result and how long the call took

### REQ-4: Run the tool server in the sandbox, once per call

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A harness outside the sandbox works in it over MCP

1. **developer** creates a fork with a sandbox of a profile that names the tool server, and gives a harness the sandbox's MCP URL and the fork's token
2. **agent** connects to POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/mcp, initializes and lists the tools
3. **parleyd** decides the full set for the token, reads the definitions from the tool server once and answers thirteen tools
4. **agent** calls code_search twice, then edit_file, then execute
5. **parleyd** for each call uploads the request file, runs the tool server on it through the runtime, answers the result, removes the file and emits one parley.sandbox.tool_call event
6. **OpenShell gateway** runs each tool server process in the sandbox's working directory as the workload user
7. **developer** reads one event per call on the event stream, and finds the edit in the working directory and no request file or index inside it

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router and pipeline, sandbox service and its gate, MCP server of the SDK, event component, store, the fake runtime with host directories

**Setup:**

- a hub started as startSandboxUseHub does, with a profile that names a tool server, hub_access = "fork" and max_concurrent_execs above 1
- the stand-in tool server answers the runtime's commands: tools prints thirteen definitions, call edit_file changes the named file in the working directory, call code_search writes under its --index-dir when the index is missing and reports whether it built it

**End state:**

- the MCP client of the SDK, given only the URL and the fork's token, listed thirteen tools
- the second code_search reported that it did not build the index
- GET /events as the developer holds four parley.sandbox.tool_call events for the sandbox, with via mcp and set full, in the order of the calls
- the file edit_file changed holds the edit, and the runtime's Walk of /workspace names no path of parley-tools
- the runtime's Walk of /tmp/parley-tools/requests is empty

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go beside TestSandboxUse_AnAgentUploadsAScriptRunsItAndDownloadsItsResult: c = an MCP client of the SDK over streamable HTTP with the bearer token; tools = c.ListTools(); len(tools) == 13; c.CallTool(code_search) twice; c.CallTool(edit_file); c.CallTool(execute); then assert the end state through GET /events and the fake's files
```

### PATH-2: A reviewer reads a colleague's sandbox over REST and cannot change it

1. **developer** as an org member with read access, requests GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools of a colleague's sandbox
2. **parleyd** decides the read-only set and answers the definitions of the tool server under --read-only
3. **developer** calls POST …/tools/read_file with a path, and then POST …/tools/execute
4. **parleyd** runs the tool server with --read-only for read_file and answers its result, and refuses execute with 403 insufficient_scope without running anything
5. **OpenShell gateway** runs the one tool server process of the read_file call

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router and pipeline, workspace access decision, sandbox service and its gate, event component, store, the fake runtime with host directories

**Setup:**

- the hub of PATH-1, a file a.txt in the working directory, and a second user who is a member of the org with read access to the fork, with an API key

**End state:**

- the listing answered set read_only without write_file, edit_file, execute and run_command
- read_file answered 200 with ok true and the content of a.txt in data
- execute answered 403 insufficient_scope
- the runtime ran the tool server's call once, with --read-only
- one parley.sandbox.tool_call event exists, for read_file, with set read_only and via rest

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: list = GET …/tools as the member; r = POST …/tools/read_file {"input": {"path": "a.txt"}}; x = POST …/tools/execute {"input": {"command": "id"}}; assert the end state
```

### PATH-3: A script searches a sandbox over REST, and a sandbox without tools refuses it

1. **agent** as a CI script with an API key, calls POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools/search_files with a pattern
2. **parleyd** runs the tool server in the sandbox and answers 200 with the matches in data
3. **agent** makes the same call, and the listing and the MCP initialize, on a sandbox of a profile without tool_server
4. **parleyd** answers each 404 tools_unavailable and runs nothing, while an exec in that sandbox still works

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router and pipeline, configuration loader with two profiles, sandbox service and its gate, store, the fake runtime with host directories

**Setup:**

- a hub with the profile tools, which names a tool server, and the profile plain, which does not, and one ready sandbox of each

**End state:**

- the search answered 200 with ok true and the stand-in's matches in data
- GET /sandbox-profiles shows tools true for tools and false for plain, and the two sandbox objects show the same
- the three routes on the plain sandbox answered 404 tools_unavailable
- POST …/exec on the plain sandbox answered 200

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: r = POST …/tools/search_files {"input": {"pattern": "TODO"}} on the tools sandbox; then GET …/tools, POST …/tools/search_files and POST …/mcp on the plain sandbox; then POST …/exec on it; assert the end state
```

## Dependencies

- `44` — uses the profiles and their validation, the profile list, the runtime client with Exec, ExecStream and Upload and its fake, the [sandbox] limits, the route declaration with the feature check, the no-widening decision and the runtime-error answer
- `45` — uses the sandbox record with the snapshot of its profile, the sandbox object and the function that scrubs a text of a sandbox's secret values
- `46` — adds its routes to the gate of the routes that use a sandbox, shares the count of concurrent execs with exec, runs a call as the collected exec runs a command, and records activity as it does
- `47` — relies on the transitions out of and back into ready, after which the tool definitions are read again, and on the checkpoint of the working directory, which the scratch directory stays out of
- `52` — emits parley.sandbox.tool_call through the event component, with the workspace's visibility

**Criteria:** REQ-2, REQ-3.4, REQ-3.5, REQ-3.6, REQ-3.7, REQ-3.8, REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2, REQ-4.3, REQ-4.4, REQ-4.5, REQ-4.6, REQ-4.7

- 3.2 Declare POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name as a tool entry of the gate, of the read kind, in state ready only, with a body limit of 8 MiB
- 3.3 Validate the body before the state check: absent or a JSON object whose input, when present, is a JSON object and whose timeout, when present, is a positive duration of the hub's duration grammar; 400 invalid_request naming the member otherwise. An input over 4 MiB as JSON is 413 payload_too_large

- 3.6 In it, take a place in the counter the exec route counts in, and refuse with the limit's refusal when none is left; give the place back when the call ends, however it ends
- 3.7 Upload {"name", "input"} to /tmp/parley-tools/requests/<32 hex characters from crypto/rand>.json with mode 0600, then run the tool server's call command through ExecStream in /workspace with no standard input and no environment, collecting standard output up to 4 MiB and one more byte, under a timer of the bound on the hub's timers, as the collected exec does
- 3.8 Take a standard output that is one JSON object with a boolean ok as the tool's result, whatever ok says. Exit status other than 0, any other output, more than 4 MiB, or a command that could not be started is a failed call, tool_server_failed, with the scrubbed message of the listing; a runtime failure is sandbox_runtime_error
- 3.9 When the timer fires, end the command's context and return the result {ok: false, error: "timeout", data: {}}
- 3.10 After the command ended, remove the request file with the runtime's Exec of rm -f on it, under a context the caller's leaving does not end; log a failed removal as a warning with the sandbox id and change nothing else
- 3.11 Record the call's start and its end as activity of the sandbox with the touch the exec route uses; a call is not an exec operation, so the observers are not told and parley_sandbox_exec_total does not count it
- 3.12 Answer the REST call 200 with ok, data, error, detail, text where the tool server gave them, and duration_ms on the hub's clock; describe the route and tool_not_found in docs/api.md
